The Revenue System Model

# Six layers. One connected revenue system.

The model separates the operating layers of revenue without treating them as independent functions. Each layer depends on the quality of the one before it. Revenue is the observable outcome.

<a href="/assessment.html" class="button">Assess your system</a><a href="/learn.html" class="text-link">Read the foundation guide →</a>

[Strategy](#strategy)[Process](#process)[CRM](#crm)[Data](#data)[Automation](#automation)[AI](#ai)[Revenue](#revenue)

01

## Strategy

Strategy defines who the system is built to serve, what value it creates and where the organisation will focus. It establishes the commercial choices that every downstream layer must support.

### Failure signals

- Everyone is a potential customer
- Priorities change by channel or team
- Activity is mistaken for progress

02

## Process

Process turns commercial choices into repeatable work. It defines stages, decisions, ownership and hand-offs across the full customer lifecycle.

### Failure signals

- Stages mean different things to different teams
- Critical work depends on individual memory
- Hand-offs create delay and lost context

03

## CRM

CRM is the operational expression of the process: the shared environment in which work, evidence and next actions become visible. Adoption follows usefulness and design.

### Failure signals

- The CRM records history but does not guide work
- Teams maintain private spreadsheets
- Required fields do not support decisions

04

## Data

Data makes system behaviour measurable. It needs common definitions, reliable capture and a clear relationship to the decisions the organisation must make.

### Failure signals

- Reports disagree on basic numbers
- Metrics describe volume without quality
- Teams debate data instead of decisions

05

## Automation

Automation removes delay and manual repetition from a process that is already understood. It scales operating discipline; it cannot create it.

### Failure signals

- Automations reproduce unclear rules
- Exceptions accumulate without ownership
- Tools add activity but little capacity

06

## AI

AI adds interpretation, generation and adaptive action where the system has sufficient context, quality and governance. Its value depends on the maturity of every previous layer.

### Failure signals

- AI tools operate outside core workflows
- Outputs lack trusted context
- Experiments have no operational owner

Outcome

## Revenue

Revenue is not the seventh function. It is the output of the entire system: the result of connected choices, behaviours, information and leverage.

### What to observe

- Conversion across the full lifecycle
- Speed, predictability and quality
- Retention, expansion and learning

Apply the model
